note: Movement catalogue for the Ironlog exercise system. A logged set references a LEAF — movement + equipment + execution + attachment — not a name string. Aliases are historical/colloquial names used for import resolution only, never for identity, and each may pin the axes its name implies (e.g. "Smith Shrug" pins equipment=smith). Axes an alias does not pin fall back to the movement defaults. `metric` omitted means reps_weight. `verified:true` means the leaf mapping was checked against real logged data; false means generated and provisional. See docs/exercise-system-phase1.md.

load.rule: per_side when execution is unilateral or alternating; else per_side when equipment is dumbbells or kettlebell and the movement is not singleImplement; else total
load.note: A bilateral dumbbell bench with two 40 kg dumbbells is logged as 40, not 80. singleImplement:true marks movements where both hands share one implement (goblet squat, pullover, Russian twist), which are total. A movement may override with loadOverride. Volume must account for this: a per_side set of 20 kg x 10 is 400 kg, not 200.

vocabularies.modifierNote: splitsPR:false annotates a set without changing identity — same leaf, same PR pool. splitsPR:true is a materially different lift and forms its own leaf; it must never share a PR pool with the unmodified version. detect terms are matched case-insensitively on whole words against the entry note; matching is literal, never fuzzy. Modifiers are extracted from notes; notes are never rewritten. Deficit / block / rack pull / board press are deliberately NOT modifiers — see the movement-vs-modifier ruling in docs/exercise-system-phase1.md section 8.
vocabularies.attachmentNote: attachments lists what a movement CAN take. What it may take on a given leaf is attachmentApplies[equipment]: "any" = every listed attachment, "bar" = only attachmentKind "bar" (a real weighted bar), "none" = attachment is always "none". Equipment absent from attachmentApplies uses _default. This is why attachment is the fourth axis of the leaf and not a movement-level field.
